title: Composition of the functors induced by exact functors on unbounded derived categories
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B},Q_{\mathcal C}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be additive functors preserving finite limits and finite colimits. Write $C(H)$ for termwise application of an additive functor $H$ to cochain complexes. For each exact $H$ write $D(H)$ for the induced derived functor, with factorization $a_H:D(H)Q\xrightarrow{\sim}QC(H)$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$\mu_{F,G}:D(GF)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(G)D(F)$$
such that, for every cochain complex $K$ of $\mathcal A$,
$$a_{G,C(F)K}\circ D(G)(a_{F,K})\circ\mu_{F,G,Q_{\mathcal A}K}=a_{GF,K},$$
where $C(G)C(F)=C(GF)$ is the termwise identity identification.

source.place: Tag 04VG, label lemma-properties-left-localization, the functor-factorization universal property. The natural-isomorphism enhancement is the fully faithful precomposition statement of Mathlib CategoryTheory.Localization.fullyFaithfulWhiskeringLeft (Predicate.lean:278) and liftNatIso (Predicate.lean:357); applied to the exact termwise derived factorizations. See report.md for the complete short proof and the existing project declaration.

proof.text: The composite $GF$ is additive and exact: applying $F$ and then $G$ preserves each finite limiting or colimiting cone. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] applies to $F$, $G$ and $GF$, giving their stated factorizations; moreover $Q_{\mathcal C}C(GF)$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms.

Put $T=D(G)D(F)$ and $H=Q_{\mathcal C}C(GF)$. Compose the whiskerings of the natural isomorphisms supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to obtain $\beta:TQ_{\mathcal A}\xrightarrow{\sim}H$, with $\beta_K=a_{G,C(F)K}\circ D(G)(a_{F,K})$. This is well typed because $a_{F,K}$ ends in $Q_{\mathcal B}C(F)K$. Termwise, both $C(G)C(F)K$ and $C(GF)K$ have object $G(F(K^r))$ and differential $G(F(d_K^r))$, and agree on maps. Hence the final identification is the identity.

By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q_{\mathcal A}$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] with $F_1=F_2=H$, $F_1\prime=D(GF)$, $F_2\prime=T$, $\phi_1=a_{GF}$, $\phi_2=\beta$ and $\tau=\mathrm{id}_H$. The identity is an isomorphism, so its lift is a natural isomorphism $\mu:D(GF)\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ satisfying $\mu_{Q_{\mathcal A}K}=\beta_K^{-1}a_{GF,K}$. Multiplying by $\beta_K$ gives exactly the required equation.

If another natural isomorphism $\nu$ satisfies the equation, cancel the isomorphism $\beta_K$ to get $\nu_{Q_{\mathcal A}K}=\beta_K^{-1}a_{GF,K}=\mu_{Q_{\mathcal A}K}$ for every $K$. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] then gives equality of the natural transformations. Their inverse transformations are equal as well, since inverses are unique, proving uniqueness of the natural isomorphism.
